input.quote: Upon the effective date of termination of participation of a Party, Schedules of this Agreement shall be appropriately modified. The remaining Parties to this Agreement shall assume the obligations, capital, operation, and maintenance interests of the Party terminating its participation in proportion to their interests assigned immediately preceding such effective date of termination, except for the continuing rights and obligations of the terminating Party as specified in Subparagraph 18.7 of this Agreement.
input.rationale:
The TRANSITION rule is scoped by its detection guidance to services/hosting agreements ("Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert)"). This instrument is not one: it is a multiparty APCN 2 construction and maintenance / co-ownership agreement among consortium Parties, in which Teleglobe USA Inc. is one of several co-owning Parties rather than a customer receiving hosted services. There is no vendor-customer relationship and no defined "Customer Data" or vendor-held customer data set — §31.1 treats "all data and information ... acquired or received by any Party" as mutual consortium confidential information, and the record-keeping obligations in §9 and §10 (p0166, p0177) are reciprocal retention/audit duties running to all Parties, not custody of our data by a supplier.

Post-exit mechanics do exist and are handled on a consortium model rather than a vendor-exit model: §18.5 (p0232) reallocates the terminating Party's interests and obligations; §18.4 (p0231) requires the remaining Parties and a terminating Terminal Party to negotiate a reasonable agreement to ensure continuous operation of that Terminal Station after the Initial Period — the functional analogue of transition assistance; §18.6 (p0234) governs liquidation/realization of assets within one year and requires the Parties to execute transfer documents; §18.7 (p0235) and §32.6 (p0280) preserve accrued liabilities; and §31.4 (p0274) keeps confidentiality alive for five years after termination.

What is genuinely absent is a data return/export in machine-readable format and a certified-deletion obligation. I have not treated that as a "missing" deviation because there is no counterparty holding our data in the sense the rule contemplates, and inserting a Vendor-facing return-and-delete covenant would be directionally wrong here: every Party (including us, as a Party that keeps books, records and maintenance records for other Parties' benefit under §9 and §10) would be equally bound, and a deletion covenant would cut against the long retention and audit rights we hold under §9.8 and §10 and the five-year confidentiality tail. Proposing the model language would therefore create an obligation on us rather than a protection for us.

Flagging for human confirmation rather than auto-closing: if the deal team considers any Party (e.g., the Network Administrator or Central Billing Party under Annexes 3 and 4) to hold Teleglobe operational or billing data in a custodial capacity, a narrow, mutual copy-out right on exit could be added to §18 — but that should be a deliberate consortium-level amendment, not a unilateral vendor-exit insert.
